scenario: You receive this text message on your phone.

content.text: Dear Customer, your SBI YONO account will be blocked today. Update your PAN card immediately: http://sbi-yono-kyc.co.in/update to avoid suspension.

explanation: Banks never ask you to update KYC/PAN through a link in an SMS. The domain 'sbi-yono-kyc.co.in' is not SBI's (onlinesbi.sbi).
clues: Threat: account will be blocked today

scenario: You just ordered food and get this SMS.

content.text: Your Swiggy order #48213 has been picked up by Ramesh and will arrive in 22 mins. Track it in the Swiggy app.

explanation: It matches something you just did, contains no link, and asks for nothing. It only points you to the official app.
clues: Expected: you just placed an order
No request for data or money

scenario: This email lands in your work inbox.

content.subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Password expires in 2 hours
content.body:
Dear User,

Your Office 365 password will expire in 2 hours. To keep the same password click below and verify your login details.

[ Keep My Password ]

Failure to verify will result in loss of email access.

Microsoft Security Team

explanation: The sender domain uses a zero instead of 'o' (micros0ft), the greeting is generic, and it threatens loss of access to rush you into entering your password.
clues: Asks you to 'verify your login details'

scenario: Your manager's name appears as the sender.

content.subject: Quick favour - confidential
content.body:
Hi,

Are you at your desk? I'm in a meeting and need you to buy 5 Amazon gift cards of Rs 10,000 each for a client. Keep this between us for now. Send me the codes by email, I'll reimburse you today.

Priya
Sent from my iPhone

explanation: This is Business Email Compromise (CEO fraud). Executives don't ask staff to buy gift cards from personal Gmail accounts, and the request for secrecy stops you from checking.
clues: Company CEO using a gmail.com address

scenario: You signed up for a GitHub account yesterday.

content.subject: [GitHub] Please verify your email address
content.body:
Hi alex-dev,

Please verify your email address so we know it's really you. Visit your GitHub settings or use the link below:
https://github.com/users/alex-dev/emails/verify

If you didn't create an account, you can ignore this email.

Thanks,
The GitHub Team

explanation: Expected after a sign-up, it addresses you by username, the link goes to github.com itself, and it lets you ignore it with no threats.

scenario: Which of these links is safe to log in to PayPal? You're shown this one:
explanation: Read domains from right to left: the real domain is 'secure-login-verify.xyz'. 'paypal.com' is only a subdomain prefix, and the link has no HTTPS.

scenario: A friend shares this link to a Python tutorial.
explanation: The registered domain is python.org, the official Python site, over HTTPS with a clean, readable path.

scenario: A pop-up says your Amazon parcel is held. The link is:
explanation: Fake delivery fees are a top smishing scam. 'amaz0n' uses a zero, the TLD is .top, and asking for a small fee is meant to steal card details.

scenario: You're selling a sofa on OLX. The 'buyer' sends this QR and says: 'Scan it to RECEIVE Rs 4,999 advance.'
explanation: UPI QR codes only SEND money. You never scan a QR or enter your UPI PIN to receive money. This QR asks you to pay Rs 4,999 to a stranger.
clues: UPI 'pay' request disguised as a refund

scenario: A sticker on a parking meter says 'Scan to pay parking'. It decodes to:
explanation: 'Quishing' stickers are pasted over real QR codes. A URL shortener hides the destination, and there's no HTTPS. Pay through the official parking app instead.

content.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the sink, this is my new number. Can you transfer Rs 15,000 urgently? I need to pay a bill today, will explain later! Don't call, my mic is broken

explanation: The 'Hi Mum/Dad' scam. A new number, an urgent money request and 'don't call' are all there to stop you verifying. Call the real number you already have.
clues: Unknown/foreign number claiming to be family

scenario: You are logging in to your bank app right now.

content.text: 248913 is your OTP for login to HDFC Bank NetBanking. Valid for 5 mins. Do not share this OTP with anyone. -HDFC Bank

explanation: An OTP you requested, with a warning not to share it. Legitimate. The danger comes if someone then CALLS asking you to read it out.

scenario: Email from an address you don't recognise.

content.subject: Tax Refund of Rs 18,450 Approved
content.body:
Dear Taxpayer,

After the last annual calculation you are eligible to receive a tax refund of Rs 18,450. Please submit the refund form with your bank account and debit card details within 48 hours.

Download: Refund_Form.html

Income Tax Department

explanation: Government sites end in .gov.in. Real refunds go to your pre-validated bank account automatically, and a .html attachment is a classic credential-harvesting form.

explanation: Real companies don't host login pages on bare IP addresses. The brand name only appears in the path.
